name: Chronicle
verdict_reason: The README claims a few dozen nanoseconds per message but publishes no benchmark, no baseline numbers and no hardware. The author also says the library is an experiment that is not complete or ready for use.
tier_reason: First-party per-message figure with no harness, hardware or comparison numbers.
claimed_speedup: 'just a few dozen nanoseconds per message' (no baseline measured)
one_liner: Experimental in-process structured logger claiming a few dozen nanoseconds per message; no published comparison with os_log or print.
how_it_is_fast: A #log macro and inlining turn each call into direct writes into a memory-mapped ring buffer, with no system call or XPC per message. Constant strings are recorded as offsets into the binary rather than copied, and only typed arguments plus a timestamp and logger ID are written. Formatting happens later, when the log is read.
use_it_when: Studying how to build a low-overhead, crash-durable in-process log
Very high message rates where os_log might drop messages, if you accept experimental code
skip_it_when: Production apps: the author says it is not complete or ready for use
You need Console.app, Instruments or sysdiagnose integration
You need a license to ship it: the repository has none
caveats: No benchmark code or numbers in the repository text beyond the one README figure
No license file, so the code is study-only
tradeoffs: Logs live in your own file; no system-wide collection or Apple tooling
Only simple integer, floating-point, Bool and String arguments can be logged

evidence.quote: With logging this cheap (just a few dozen nanoseconds per message!) there's no reason to turn it off.
Complete or ready for use. See below.
